content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT opened: GPU-DECODE-STREAM-OOM — multiple decode nodes reporting CUDA OOMs and client request drops

sara: saw pager alert at 08:07. decode-stream error rate up ~18% and 502/request-dropped spikes. throwing OOMs on nodes in us-west-2 cluster. tagging oncall.

mike_r: oncall here, ack. attaching graphs. which model family? any customer impact reported yet?

sara: primarily streaming endpoints for llama-2-13B-quant variants. telemetry shows a cluster of requests with very large `max_tokens` headers (some > 50k).

jia: looking at node logs now. getting repeated `cudaMalloc` failures then `CUDA out of memory` in decode loop. sample log:
```
2026-03-15T08:05:43Z runtime[decode]: ERROR decode_stream: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (0x2)
2026-03-15T08:05:43Z runtime[decode]: ERROR decode_stream: token loop runaway, kv_cache growth > expected, dropping request
```

ash: possible runaway generation — either client bypassed `max_tokens` or header misinterpreted. also seeing a few containers with huge KV cache footprints (30GB+).

sara: immediate ask: prevent further node OOMs and stop customer-visible drops. suggestions?

mike_r: mitigation steps: 1) enforce hard token ceiling at ingress (nginx/gateway) 2) route new streaming requests to fallback small-instance pool 3) mark affected nodes DRAIN and restart runtime. deploying step 1 now.

ash: I can push a temporary ingress header enforcement: `X-Token-Ceiling: 4096` and reject > that. will also set streaming `max_prefix_kv` to sane bounds on runtime-side. applying now.

opsbot: command run: `kubectl -n runtime annotate node node-345 avoid-scheduling=true`

opsbot: command run: `kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deploy/decode-runtime -l pool=us-west-2-streaming`

jia: doing live eviction of pods with `OOM` status, restarting cuda drivers on 3 hosts. patching kernel param to reduce memory fragmentation temporarily.

sara: traffic cutover to fallback small-instance pool is in progress, ~20% shifted. error rate dropping to 6%. customers still see increased latency on streaming but fewer dropped requests.

cs_lead: heads-up: support queue has two incoming tickets mentioning timeouts and partial responses. drafting a short customer message — "we're investigating increased errors on streaming endpoints; mitigation in progress."

mike_r: root cause triage notes: most offending requests show `max_tokens=65536` coming from a single client SDK version 0.9.1 that changed units (tokens vs. bytes). also a small regression in prefix caching that fails to trim KV after reroute. combo led to runaway KV growth during decode.

ash: created quick patch: 1) enforce server-side token ceiling in gateway (reject > 8k) 2) server-side defensive clamp in runtime `max_decode_tokens = min(requested, 8192)` 3) backpressure: disable continuous batching for streaming on fallback pool. deploying patch to canary now.

sara: canary looks good for 10 minutes (no OOMs). rolling to remaining runtime replicas.

mike_r: customer-impact assessment: ~0.9% of total requests in last 2 hours were dropped; ~12 customers saw partial responses. escalated three enterprise accounts (sent proactive emails).

cs_lead: posted proactive message to affected customers with ETA for full fix and offer to re-run failed jobs.

jia: after restart most nodes memory stabilized. collected heap/KV snapshots and saved to s3://redwood-incidents/3543210000/kv-dumps for postmortem.

ash: follow-ups I am creating: SDK patch to prevent unit-confusion, runtime regression fix for KV trim, and circuit-breaker for prefix growth. will open PRs and link them here.

mike_r: quick checklist before close: - confirm ingress ceiling deployed in all regions - confirm rollout complete and no new OOMs for 30m - postmortem scheduled - customer follow-up done

sara: ingress ceiling in all active regions: us-west-2, eu-central-1, us-east-1 ✅

opsbot: deployment status: rollout complete for `ingress-token-ceiling` across clusters.

jia: no new OOMs in 35 minutes. request error rate back to baseline. marking incident as mitigated.

incident-bot: INCIDENT `GPU-DECODE-STREAM-OOM` mitigated by oncall team. severity: sev3 -> monitoring.

cs_lead: final note to support: follow up 1:1 with the three enterprise contacts, offer credits. postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-16 14:00 UTC — owners: ash, jia, sara.

ash: thanks team. I'll file PRs and link the postmortem artifacts.

mike_r: thanks all — handing back to ops rotation.

sara: closing thread, will post postmortem link later. :white_check_mark:
